cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: string comparison with == is case-insensitive.

cases.why_hard: Values of different types are coerced before comparing: a numeric string equals the number it spells, so '1' == 1 holds even though the types differ.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: values of different types are converted to numbers before comparing; a string that is a number equals that number.

cases.why_hard: null and '' both coerce to 0 when compared, so a missing value equals an empty string, which a naive null check misses.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: null converts to 0 and an empty string to 0 when comparing values of different types.

cases.why_hard: Booleans coerce to numbers too: true compares equal to 1.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: true converts to 1 and false to 0 when comparing against a number.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: || returns the first truthy operand, not a boolean.

cases.why_hard: && also returns an operand rather than a boolean, so '' && 'x' yields the empty string, not false.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: && returns the first falsy operand, or the last operand when all are truthy.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Truthy and falsy values: the empty string is falsy.

cases.why_hard: contains() over an array compares each string item with the same case-insensitive rule as a string search.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Functions: contains(search, item) matches an array's string items case-insensitively.

cases.why_hard: {{ and }} are literal braces in format(); a single brace is a placeholder, so the braces around the value must be doubled to survive.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Functions: format() escapes a literal { as {{ and } as }}.

cases.why_hard: A placeholder with no matching argument is an error, not an empty substitution.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Functions: format() requires an argument for every placeholder index.

cases.why_hard: Malformed JSON must fail the evaluation; it must not produce null and let the job run.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Functions: fromJSON() errors on input that is not valid JSON.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions: calling a function that does not exist is an error.

cases.why_hard: The expression language has no + operator; 1 + 1 must be rejected, not evaluated as something else.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Operators: the operator list has no arithmetic operators.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Contexts: a property that is not set reads as null.

cases.why_hard: A name that is not a context at all is rejected, not read as null; a typo in a context name must not silently pass.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Contexts: only the documented contexts exist; any other named value is an error.

cases.why_hard: When no file matches, hashFiles returns the empty string, which is a value, not an error; a cache key built from it must still evaluate.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Functions: hashFiles() returns an empty string when no files match.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Status check functions: success() is false once something before has failed.

cases.why_hard: always() is the one status function true after a skipped need, so it is the only way such a job runs.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Status check functions: always() runs the job even when its needs were skipped.

cases.why_hard: A skipped need makes success() false as well, so the dependent job is skipped too instead of running.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Status check functions: success() is false when a needed job was skipped; the job then is skipped.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Status check functions: cancelled() is true when the workflow run was cancelled.

cases.why_hard: When one need failed and another was skipped, failure() is true; a skipped sibling does not hide the failure.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions > Status check functions: failure() is true when any previous step or needed job failed.
GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Jobs > jobs.<job_id>.if: a job with no needs runs under success().

cases.why_hard: A null value renders as nothing at all, so x and y are adjacent rather than separated by 'null'.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions: a null value in a string is replaced by the empty string.

cases.why_hard: An opening ${{ with no closing }} is a malformed template and must be an error, not literal text.
cases.source: GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax > Expressions: every ${{ must be closed by }}.
